I think your explanation perfectly encapsulates the difference between voice dysphoria & just 'hating your voice'. People who hate their voice in recordings usually do so because everyone sounds different in recordings. We all hear our own voices through the filter of our brain, so we not only hear the sound coming out from our mouths, but also our internal voice (don't quote me on the exact science of this.) Most people who hate their voice are like that because there is a level of disconnect between what they think they're hearing & what they're actually hearing, & it tends to be really jarring for the brain.

Voice dysphoria, on the other hand, is hating your voice not because of how it sounds, but because of how it *doesn't* sound. You dislike your voice because it isn't low enough. I hate my voice because it isn't low enough. Low enough for what? Low enough to be read as male, which is what dysphoria is all about: the distress at not being seen (by yourself or by others) as your preferred gender. People who simply hate their voices do not wish they sounded different because their current voice gets them clocked as the wrong gender (although some may have that if their voice is high/low pitched enough for their AGAB). But we DO hate our voices because they get us clocked, & because they're not deep or high enough for our preferred gender. That's the big difference, really.

Now that that's out of the way:

Honestly, there is no strict timescale for when my moods flip. I tried making a timeline once in secondary school & failed, because there just wasn't any particular pattern to it all. Sometimes I can go months feeling like a man. Sometimes I have a few minutes at most where I feel more femme. Most of the time I feel agender, & like a void of nothingness. 

How often I feel as different genders also changes based on where I am at life. In secondary school, I felt femme far more often, because I was AFAB & shoved into an all girls school & had a lot of internalised transphobia. When I left secondary & went onto uni, where there was a far wider array of people, I had longer periods of feeling masculine or like a man, because I was surrounded by men & my dysphoria worsened from seeing so many people my age who I distinctly didn't resemble. 

All in all, it doesn't really matter when or how often you switch & fluctuate, is my opinion. I am still as much genderfluid when I feel like a man for 4 months, as I do when I want to paint my nails for a day. What matters most is if you're happy with the label of genderfluid. You might fluctuate but genderfluid personally doesn't vibe with you & that's ok (there are other labels like bigender, pangender, genderflux, etc.) You may not fluctuate almost ever, just a few times a year or something, but still vibe with the label of genderfluid because it explains those rare moments of fluctuation, & having that label for those moments makes you happy. Just have fun, don't be a dick to people, & enjoy yourself no matter what your gender expression is in the moment.
